AccDSL Core 0 describes entities and books, accounts, observations, shared
unknowns, constraints, alternative interpretations, contract instances,
accounting rules and reporting mappings. It has pure expressions and a
restricted posting effect. Economic forecasting algorithms can live in typed
plugins; unrestricted numerical code does not need to be reimplemented in
the DSL. The grammar and interface details in Appendix~\ref{app:contracts}
are normative for the first parser.

The complete grammar is supplied as \code{spec/core-0.lark}, and the exact
record fields as \code{spec/core-ir.schema.json}. The companion
\code{spec/core-contract.md} defines reference resolution, expression arity,
type/context checks, operations, failures and identity. Structural schema
validation alone does not establish those semantic properties. ASCII
identifiers and UTF-8 strings are used in this revision; currency suffixes,
dates and decimal literals have explicit lexical rules. The grammar is checked
by parsing the complete demonstration file, not by claiming that its parser
also implements a compiler or solver.

\begin{lstlisting}
execute_event(event, state, run_context):
    verify prerequisites and information availability
    resolve applicable measurement and recognition rules
    compute proposed economic changes and measurements
    compute proposed journal batch(es)
    validate types, contexts, balance, constraints and idempotency
    atomically commit state, journals and explanation edges
    return new state, emitted dependent events, diagnostics
\end{lstlisting}

The official IFRS overviews for IFRS 9, IAS 32 and IFRS 17 establish the relevant
scope of financial-instrument measurement, presentation and insurance
contracts \citep{ifrs9,ias32,ifrs17}. They are orientation sources, not substitutes
for reviewed paragraph-level implementations. Public retrieval of the selected
Chinese Ministry of Finance page and SEC API documentation failed during this
campaign; the source register records these access gaps. ASBE and US GAAP
semantic modules therefore have explicit primary-text acquisition and
accounting-review tasks before they can be marked executable and compliant.

The initial implementation uses Python for orchestration and a deterministic
reference evaluator, exact decimal/rational arithmetic for booked amounts,
SQLite for transactional metadata and versioned records, and columnar files
for large scenario outputs. DuckDB is an optional analytical reader. These
are convenience choices justified by inspectability and modest initial scale;
they do not establish production performance. The IR and conformance tests
allow a later compiled executor without changing accounting meaning.

The Python and command-line interfaces expose the same operations:
\begin{lstlisting}
ingest(manifest, extractor_config) -> EvidenceVersion
compile(source_or_ir, evidence_view, package_lock) -> ModelPlan | Diagnostics
reconcile(plan, cutoff, solver_config) -> HistoryFamily | Diagnostics
condition(family, assumptions) -> ConditionalFamily | Infeasible
simulate(family, scenario_set, run_config) -> RunResult
render(run_id, report_request) -> ReportBundle
explain(node_id, evidence_view_or_run_id) -> ExplanationGraph
compare(run_a, run_b, alignment_spec) -> Comparison
\end{lstlisting}
\end{minipage}

The reference serialisation uses UTF-8 JSON with NFC strings, sorted ASCII
keys, no insignificant whitespace and no floating-point literals. Exact
numbers are reduced rational numerator/denominator strings; zero is $0/1$.
Duplicate keys, NaN, infinities and unpaired Unicode surrogates are rejected.
Arrays preserve order unless the schema declares a set, such as a constraint
conjunction or source-ID set, in which case IDs are sorted. This normalisation
recognises representational equality, not arbitrary economic equivalence.

An economic event ID derives from owner, schedule version, date, phase,
operation and occurrence ordinal. The idempotency key pairs run ID and event
ID. Identical payloads return the committed result; different payloads under
the same key produce \code{EventIdentityConflict}. Independent events
may reorder only when read/write sets are disjoint or a package proves
commutation, including funding constraints. Alphabetical ordering cannot
settle an economic timing ambiguity.

Exact method arguments and result fields are specified in
\code{spec/core-contract.md}; \path{spec/core-ir.schema.json} supplies closed
structural definitions. Every method returns a success record or a
diagnostic with code, source IDs, entity/period, dependency path and retry
status. The principal sequence is \code{ingest}, \code{review},
\code{compile}, \code{reconstruct}, \code{simulate}, \code{report}, with
\code{bound}, \code{explain} and \code{replay} over frozen identities.

The immediate implementation task is P0 using the complete Northstar and debt
fixtures, the temporal/review cases and the declared IR. Broader corporate and
sector support grows through the specified operations and reviewed examples;
no generic rule package is presumed to cover all financial statements.

The disclosure corpus grows in distinct strata: an ordinary US-GAAP issuer
(Apple, with Caterpillar as a contrasting inventory policy), an IFRS corporate
issuer, an ASBE corporate issuer, a bank and an insurer with contract-group
disclosures. The acquired Apple package is the initial real stratum, not a
representative population sample. Each later stratum requires an annual and
interim package, at least three dates, policies, note links and a changed
comparative or a documented absence of one. Synthetic restatement cases supply
controlled revisions when the real package contains none. Candidate issuer
selection, acquisition status and operations to annotate are explicit in
\code{fixtures/corpus-protocol.json}; unacquired strata remain pending.

The normative grammar is reproduced from \code{spec/core-0.lark}. Names are
case-sensitive ASCII identifiers; strings are UTF-8 with JSON escaping. All
literal words in the grammar are reserved. The companion contract specifies
valid dates, exact rational literals, argument arity, type/context checks and
package resolution. A syntax parse is not semantic validation.

The closed machine-readable definitions are in
\path{spec/core-ir.schema.json}. They define contexts, source spans,
observations, narratives, coverage units, mappings, partitions, entity/control
records, books, accounts, symbols, choices, expressions, constraints, assumptions,
alternatives, contracts, events, rules, packages, measurements, states,
journals, scenarios, information views, review decisions, evidence views,
model scopes, historical families, probability models, report mappings,
result cells, branches, runs and diagnostics. The schema is normative for
field spelling and structural shape; the semantic contract is normative for
reference resolution, units, contexts, applicability and operations.

A value is a reduced rational, or a typed symbolic/domain reference. A
posting is nonnegative with its side carrying the sign, in the book's
functional currency. Original units and the valuation reference survive
conversion. Monetary contexts require currency; a period flow requires a
calendar and exclusive end boundary. Zero postings may preserve traceability
but do not establish that an economic event occurred. The amount may have
finer precision before the declared posting-rounding operation.
